flashcard_questions.q: In which year did Margaret Thatcher become Prime Minister?
Which 1981 riots in Liverpool form part of the play’s context?
What drove the Toxteth Riots of 1981?
flashcard_questions.a: Deep unemployment and poverty in Liverpool’s working-class communities.

flashcard_questions.q: Blood Brothers was written in ____ and is set from the late 1950s to the early 1980s.
How does the police officer treat the two families differently?
flashcard_questions.a: Harshly to the working-class Johnstones but politely to the middle-class Lyons.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the central theme of Blood Brothers?
What conclusion does Russell reach in the nature versus nurture debate?
flashcard_questions.a: Nurture wins — environment, not genetics, shapes a person’s future.

flashcard_questions.q: Which bird recurs in Blood Brothers as an omen of sorrow?
Which superstition warns of bad luck in Blood Brothers?
Which film star does Mrs Johnstone sing about being compared to?
Why do bailiffs repossess Mrs Johnstone’s furniture?
flashcard_questions.a: She cannot keep up the payments on catalogue goods.

flashcard_questions.q: What is meant by catalogue debt?
flashcard_questions.a: Buying goods on credit and paying in instalments because you cannot pay upfront.

flashcard_questions.q: Which sound would a designer use for the Johnstones’ inner-city home?
flashcard_questions.a: Industrial noise from the nearby docklands.

flashcard_questions.q: Where are the Johnstones rehoused later in the play?

notes: 14 cards: 2 date cards, 1 cloze on the writing date, 4 context→effect, 3 theme cards, 2 term→definition, 2 place cards. Government welfare detail was folded into the Toxteth card; the cinema and street-play cultural notes were dropped as flavour.
